reviewContext.userProblem: On BPMN pages the opaque pool and lane bodies paint over every sequence and message flow in the ui-solid canvas and in SVG export, because isConnectorBackdrop (packages/core/src/backdrops.ts) lowers only frames beneath the connector layer; and every task type shows the same top-right placeholder square instead of a distinct BPMN marker icon at the top-left.

SVG export of the committed purchase-request fixture paints all 12 sequence flows and their arrowheads after every participant and lane body; the canvas partition uses the same predicate.
Connector routing no longer treats pools, lanes, expanded sub-processes or BPMN groups as obstacles; a collapsed sub-process still is.

designDecisionsAndRationale: Broaden the single predicate isConnectorBackdrop rather than touching its three consumers (svg-export connectorBackdropIds, Canvas.tsx backdrop layer, connector.ts obstacleBoxes), so editor, export and routing cannot diverge (design 6.4).
A collapsed (black-box) participant is also a backdrop, keeping the predicate a pure type test and ensuring it never hides a docked message flow (design 6.4).
Only expanded sub-processes are surfaces; a collapsed sub-process is a node and stays a shape and an obstacle (design 6.4).
Icons are fixed-coordinate primitives in the shared notation module so canvas and export match; one main role per icon keeps existing role-count tests unchanged (design 6.1).
Label origin uses the box origin only and export passes the resolved box, so canvas and export agree by construction (design 6.1 Labels, 6.2).
New SVG layer tests live in svg-export-layers.test.ts so the two parallel plans do not share a test file (design 11).
intentionalTradeoffs: Flows paint above pools, lanes, expanded sub-processes and groups but below flow nodes, including beneath an expanded sub-process's name and markers (design 13); bpmn-js paints connections above every shape.
Editor-authored z-order inside the backdrop layer is kept as authored (design 6.4).
The task icon may overlap the activity label on very small tasks (design 6.1).
Routing through pools and lanes may change CLI export waypoints; a failing apps/cli/src/bpmn-commands.test.ts escalates to the orchestrator without editing tests or fixtures.
supportedEdgeCases: Collapsed black-box pools with docked message flows.
Nested lanes and expanded sub-processes inside lanes, painted in page z-order (pool below lanes below sub-process).
Grouped elements (diagra group) keep group paint order and stay routing obstacles.
Pages without connectors have no backdrops.
Shapes without stored visual.x/visual.y but with labelBounds render their label at the same absolute point on canvas and in export.
visual.style.stroke overrides the filled send icon colour; visual.style.fill overrides the unfilled group body.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Reordering z-order of user-authored BPMN containers.
Painting flows above flow nodes (bpmn-js behaviour).
Icon scaling for very small tasks.
